examples.question_text: Identify any outliers in $4, 30, 32, 34, 35, 36, 38, 40, 42, 44, 70$ using the formal $1.5\times\text{IQR}$ rule. Justify your answer with calculations.
examples.solution_text:
The median is $36$. Exclude it when finding the medians of the lower and upper halves.
$Q_1=32,\quad Q_3=42$
$\begin{align*}\text{IQR}&=Q_3-Q_1\\&=42-32\\&=10\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}\text{Lower fence}&=Q_1-1.5\times\text{IQR}\\&=32-1.5\times10\\&=17\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}\text{Upper fence}&=Q_3+1.5\times\text{IQR}\\&=42+1.5\times10\\&=57\end{align*}$
Since $4<17$ and $70>57$, $4$ and $70$ are outliers. All other values lie within the fences.

examples.question_text: The heights, in centimetres, of twelve plants are $10, 30, 32, 34, 35, 36, 38, 40, 42, 44, 46, 72$. Find both fences and identify any outliers.
examples.solution_text:
Split the ordered data into two halves of six values. Each quartile is the mean of the two middle values in its half.
$\begin{align*}Q_1&=\frac{32+34}{2}\\&=33\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}Q_3&=\frac{42+44}{2}\\&=43\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}\text{IQR}&=43-33\\&=10\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}\text{Lower fence}&=33-1.5\times10\\&=18\text{ cm}\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}\text{Upper fence}&=43+1.5\times10\\&=58\text{ cm}\end{align*}$
Since $10<18$ and $72>58$, the heights $10\text{ cm}$ and $72\text{ cm}$ are outliers. All other heights lie within the fences.

examples.question_text: A dataset has five-number summary $\text{Min}=3,\ Q_1=18,\ Q_2=24,\ Q_3=30,\ \text{Max}=48$. Determine whether it contains any outliers.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{align*}\text{IQR}&=30-18\\&=12\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}\text{Lower fence}&=18-1.5\times12\\&=0\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}\text{Upper fence}&=30+1.5\times12\\&=48\end{align*}$
The minimum satisfies $3\ge0$, and the maximum equals the upper fence of $48$. There are no outliers: a value must lie strictly beyond a fence.

examples.question_text: A dataset has $Q_1=20$ and $Q_3=32$. What is its maximum possible range if there are no outliers?
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{align*}\text{IQR}&=32-20\\&=12\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}\text{Lower fence}&=20-1.5\times12\\&=2\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}\text{Upper fence}&=32+1.5\times12\\&=50\end{align*}$
Values equal to the fences are allowed. The greatest range occurs when the minimum is $2$ and the maximum is $50$.
$\begin{align*}\text{Maximum possible range}&=50-2\\&=48\end{align*}$

examples.derivation: The sixth value is 36. Excluding it leaves five values in each half, whose medians are 32 and 42. IQR = 10; lower fence = 32 − 15 = 17; upper fence = 42 + 15 = 57. Only 4 and 70 lie strictly beyond the fences.
The lower six values give Q1 = (32 + 34)/2 = 33; the upper six give Q3 = (42 + 44)/2 = 43. IQR = 10; fences are 18 cm and 58 cm. Only 10 cm and 72 cm are outliers.
IQR = 30 − 18 = 12. The fences are 18 − 18 = 0 and 30 + 18 = 48. The minimum 3 is inside the fences and the maximum 48 equals the upper fence, so there are no outliers.
IQR = 32 − 20 = 12. The fences are 2 and 50. Both endpoints are permitted, so the maximum possible range is 50 − 2 = 48. These endpoints are compatible with the supplied quartiles.
